title: First Amended Petition to Contest Will and for Declaratory Judgment
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN RE: ESTATE OF MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. PR-2024-0789

FIRST AMENDED PETITION TO CONTEST WILL AND FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, CLINTON J. BARNES, individually and as a beneficiary under the purported Last Will and Testament of MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, Deceased, and files this First Amended Petition to Contest Will and for Declaratory Judgment, and in support thereof respectfully shows the Court as follows:

I. PARTIES

1. Petitioner CLINTON J. BARNES (hereinafter "Clint" or "Mr. Barnes") is an individual residing in Bastrop County, Texas, and is the nephew of the Decedent.

2. Respondent, VIVIAN HARTWELL-STERLING (hereinafter "Ms. Hartwell-Sterling" or "Vivian"), is an individual residing in Dallas County, Texas, and is the named independent executrix under the purported Will. Vivian is also a niece of the Decedent.

3. The Decedent, MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, died on or about March 12, 2024, a resident of Travis County, Texas.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

4. This Court has jurisdiction over this proceeding pursuant to Texas Estates Code § 32.001 ("The probate court has jurisdiction over all probate matters..."). Venue is proper in Travis County because the Decedent resided here at the time of her death.

III. FACTS

5. On April 10, 2024, Vivian filed an Application for Probate of Will and Issuance of Letters Testamentary, alleging that a document dated March 1, 2024, is the Last Will of Margaret Louise Hartwell. The purported Will leaves the bulk of the estate, valued at approximately $2.3 million, to Vivian and her brother, ROGER HARTWELL (hereinafter "Roger" or "Mr. Hartwell"). Clint received only a bequest of $5,000.

6. Clint contests the March 1, 2024 document on grounds of lack of testamentary capacity, undue influence by Vivian and Roger, and improper execution. The Decedent was 89 years old and suffered from advanced dementia. She was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in 2019. Her primary care physician, Dr. Susan K. Reeves, noted in records dated February 15, 2024, that "the patient is unable to manage her own affairs."

7. The purported Will was witnessed by two individuals: JANE DOE (a certified nursing assistant employed by Vivian) and JOHN SMITH (a neighbor who is legally blind). Neither witness had any prior relationship with the Decedent.

8. On October 22, 2024, the Court held a status conference. The Honorable Judge LUCIA A. RAMIREZ presided. During the conference, counsel for Vivian, Attorney MICHAEL THOMPSON of Thompson & Associates, PLLC, argued that the Will should be admitted to probate summarily. Counsel for Clint, Attorney REBECCA CHEN of Chen & Lee, LLP, objected and requested discovery.

9. The Decedent's Social Security number is 456-78-1234. The Decedent's date of birth was April 17, 1935.

10. The minor child of Clint, identified as A.B., is a contingent beneficiary under a prior Will dated July 12, 2018, which Clint seeks to probate in the alternative.

11. The Decedent maintained a phone number of 512-555-0198 and an email address of mlhartwell@mailfict.com.

12. Roger Hartwell resides at 742 Elm Street, Austin, Texas 78701. Clint Barnes resides at 1886 Oak Lane, Bastrop, Texas 78602.

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION

13. Lack of Testamentary Capacity. The Decedent lacked the mental capacity to execute a Will on March 1, 2024. See In re: Estate of Elkins, 987 S.W.2d 876, 880 (Tex. App.—Austin 1998) ("The testator must have sufficient mental ability to understand the nature of his act, the nature and extent of his property, and the natural objects of his bounty."). Further, the case of Hartwell v. Barnes, 789 S.W.3d 456, 462 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2023), held that a diagnosis of dementia creates a presumption of incapacity.

14. Undue Influence. Vivian and Roger exerted undue influence over the Decedent by isolating her from Clint and controlling her medications. See Prado v. Prado, 456 S.W.3d 789, 795 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2015).

15. Improper Execution. The Will does not comply with Texas Estates Code § 251.051, which requires that "the testator must sign the will in the presence of two or more credible witnesses." The witnesses here were not credible.

V. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Petitioner prays that the Court set aside the purported Will of March 1, 2024, declare it void, admit the prior Will of July 12, 2018, to probate, and award such other relief as is just.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Rebecca Chen
REBECCA CHEN
Chen & Lee, LLP
123 Congress Avenue, Suite 400
Austin, Texas 78701
Phone: 512-555-0234
Email: rchen@chenlee-law.com
State Bar No. 24056789

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true copy of the foregoing was served on Michael Thompson, counsel for Respondent, on November 1, 2024.

/s/ Rebecca Chen

title: Respondent's Original Answer and Counterclaim to Contest Will
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN RE: ESTATE OF MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. PR-2024-0789

RESPONDENT'S ORIGINAL ANSWER AND COUNTERCLAIM

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, VIVIAN HARTWELL-STERLING (hereinafter "Vivian" or "Ms. Hartwell-Sterling"), Respondent and Counterclaimant, and files this Original Answer and Counterclaim to the Petition filed by CLINTON J. BARNES (hereinafter "Clint" or "Mr. Barnes"), and respectfully shows the Court as follows:

I. ANSWER

1. Respondent denies each and every allegation in the First Amended Petition, except as specifically admitted herein.

2. Respondent admits that the Decedent, Margaret Louise Hartwell, died on March 12, 2024, and that her Social Security number was 456 78 1234. Respondent further admits that the Decedent's date of birth was April 17, 1935, and her phone number was 512-555-0198 and email mlhartwell@mailfict.com.

3. Respondent admits that the purported Will dated March 1, 2024, was offered for probate, but denies that it is invalid. The Will was executed in the presence of two credible witnesses, JANE DOE and JOHN SMITH, and complies with Texas Estates Code § 251.051 ("The testator must sign the will in the presence of two or more credible witnesses.").

II. AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES

4. The Decedent had full testamentary capacity on March 1, 2024. Contrary to Clint's allegations, Dr. Susan K. Reeves's records were taken out of context. Dr. Reeves later stated in a deposition that the Decedent had lucid intervals. See In re: Estate of Elkins, 987 S.W.2d 876 (Tex. App.—Austin 1998).

5. No undue influence occurred. The Decedent expressed a clear desire to favor Vivian and Roger because they cared for her in her final years. The case of Hartwell v. Barnes, 789 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2023), is distinguishable because that case involved a paid caregiver.

III. COUNTERCLAIM FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT

6. Respondent seeks a declaratory judgment that the March 1, 2024 Will is valid and that the prior Will dated July 12, 2018, is revoked. The minor child A.B. has no standing to contest the Will.

IV. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Respondent prays that the Court deny Clint's petition, admit the March 1, 2024 Will to probate, and declare it valid.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Michael Thompson
MICHAEL THOMPSON
Thompson & Associates, PLLC
456 Guadalupe Street, Suite 200
Austin, Texas 78701
Phone: 512-555-0456
Email: mthompson@thompsonassociates.com
State Bar No. 24098765

/s/ Michael Thompson

title: Order Denying Motion for Summary Judgment
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN RE: ESTATE OF MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, DECEASED

CAUSE NO. PR-2024-0789

ORDER DENYING MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT

On this day, the Court considered Counterclaimant Vivian Hartwell-Sterling's Motion for Summary Judgment. The Honorable LUCIA A. RAMIREZ, Judge Presiding, has reviewed the pleadings, evidence, and arguments of counsel. The Court finds that genuine issues of material fact exist regarding the Decedent's testamentary capacity and the credibility of witnesses. The Motion is DENIED.

It is further ORDERED that discovery shall proceed. The Court notes the standard set forth in In re: Estate of Elkins, 987 S.W.2d 876 (Tex. App.—Austin 1998), and Hartwell v. Barnes, 789 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2023). The Court also cites the relevant statute, Texas Estates Code § 251.051, which requires credible witnesses.

The minor A.B. is not a party to this motion.

SIGNED this 20th day of November, 2024.

/s/ Lucia A. Ramirez
LUCIA A. RAMIREZ
JUDGE PRESIDING

title: Motion to Compel Discovery and for Sanctions
text:
IN THE PROBATE COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN RE: ESTATE OF MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, DECEASED

DOCKET NO. PR-2024-0789

MOTION TO COMPEL DISCOVERY AND FOR SANCTIONS

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, CLINTON J. BARNES ("Clint" or "Mr. Barnes"), by and through his attorney of record, REBECCA CHEN of Chen & Lee, LLP, and files this Motion to Compel Discovery and for Sanctions against Respondent VIVIAN HARTWELL-STERLING ("Vivian" or "Ms. Hartwell-Sterling"), and in support thereof states:

I. BACKGROUND

1. This is a will contest regarding the Estate of MARGARET LOUISE HARTWELL, Deceased, who died on March 12, 2024. Her Social Security number was 456-78-1234, date of birth April 17, 1935.

2. On October 15, 2024, Clint served interrogatories and requests for production on Vivian. Vivian failed to respond by November 15, 2024. Counsel, MICHAEL THOMPSON of Thompson & Associates, PLLC, has not provided any explanation.

3. The requested discovery includes: (a) communications between Vivian and the Decedent in the 90 days before the Will's execution; (b) medical records of the Decedent from January 1, 2023 to death; (c) phone records for 512-555-0198; (d) email records for mlhartwell@mailfict.com; and (e) financial records regarding Roger Hartwell.

II. LEGAL STANDARD

4. Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 192.4 requires full discovery. The Court may impose sanctions under Texas Estates Code § 55.001. See also In re: Estate of Elkins, 987 S.W.2d 876 (Tex. App.—Austin 1998).

III. ARGUMENT

5. Vivian's failure to respond is willful. The minor A.B. has an interest in the estate, and delay prejudices all parties.

IV. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Clint moves the Court to compel Vivian to respond within 10 days and award sanctions including attorney's fees.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Rebecca Chen
REBECCA CHEN
Chen & Lee, LLP
123 Congress Avenue, Suite 400
Austin, Texas 78701
Phone: 512-555-0234
Email: rchen@chenlee-law.com
State Bar No. 24056789

/s/ Rebecca Chen
